PhD in Chemical Engineering
The PhD in Chemical Engineering at Lehigh University’s P.C. Rossin College of Engineering and Applied Science is a research doctorate housed in the Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering, with specializations spanning energy, biomolecular science, functional materials, interfacial science, molecular simulation and data science.

Overview
What the PhD in Chemical Engineering is
Lehigh’s Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering offers a vibrant education and research environment with opportunities to specialize in research spanning areas of energy and the environment, biomolecular sciences, functional materials and nanotechnology, colloidal and interfacial science, molecular modeling and simulations, and data science, systems, and controls.
Research approaches include experiments, modeling, simulation, and theory, and combinations thereof. The department has 16 tenured and tenure-track faculty — 10 full professors, four associate professors and two assistant professors — plus one associate teaching faculty member.
The department was ranked 22nd overall in the most recent (2010) decennial National Research Council report, and previously ranked 5th nationally in the High-Impact Chemical Engineering Department Ranking, 1996–2000.
The Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering maintains the authoritative program detail — see the department page.

Degree requirements
What the doctorate requires
Lehigh publishes the following requirements for the PhD in Chemical Engineering.
Coursework
All PhD students complete eight courses in consultation with their committee. CHE 400, CHE 410, CHE 415 and CHE 452 are required.
Qualifying examination
All PhD students must pass a qualification examination given during the second year of residence.
Dissertation
The program culminates in doctoral dissertation research. Detailed procedures are set out in the department’s PhD Guidelines and Procedures.
The catalog does not state a total credit-hour figure for the Chemical Engineering PhD; consult the department’s PhD Guidelines and Procedures.

Funding
Financial support
All PhDs at the Rossin College are 100% fully-funded, however, funding sources may vary by department. Funding covers PhD tuition and a stipend.
The Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering does not publish program-specific stipend or assistantship figures; ask the graduate contact below what funding looks like for this program.
PhD applicants wishing to be considered for financial assistance should submit a complete application no later than December 15 for a fall semester start.
Named opportunities open to Rossin College doctoral students include the Rossin Research Scholars program, Pasteur PhD Partners (P3), and the SEED-EF NSF National Research Traineeship — see special opportunities for Lehigh PhD students.
Financial aid for Lehigh’s graduate programs consists mainly of fixed-rate federal student loans through the Office of Financial Aid.
Loan eligibility requires enrollment at least half-time — six credits during the academic year, three credits in summer.
Emergency loans and grants are available through the Graduate Life Office.

Admissions
How to apply
Applications for admission — all semesters, all levels — are completed online. Applications open September 1; PhD applications for fall admission are due December 15 for financial aid consideration.
Application open dates and deadlines are determined by individual departments. Contact the department concerning relevant deadlines and available start terms.
What to submit
Completed online application
Official transcripts (with English translation for international applicants)
Statement of purpose / essay
Letters of recommendation (typically three)
Résumé or CV
Application fee of $50 USD
Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering requirements
Prior degree: A B.S. or M.S. in chemical engineering or a related engineering discipline is required by matriculation. Related science fields are considered but are less common.
GPA: A GPA (U.S. equivalent) higher than 3.3 on a 4.0 scale is preferred.
GRE: As of Fall 2020, the Lehigh ChBE program no longer requires submission of GRE scores.
Recommendations: A minimum of two letters of recommendation; preference is given to research advisors and professors.
Deadline: For fall admission, full applications — including test scores and letters of recommendation — should be submitted no later than Dec. 15.
The GRE is not required or considered for any Rossin College graduate program.

Questions
Frequently asked questions
Which department at Lehigh offers the PhD in Chemical Engineering?
The PhD in Chemical Engineering is offered by Lehigh University’s Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering, within the P.C. Rossin College of Engineering and Applied Science. Full program detail, faculty and current requirements are maintained on the department’s own page: https://engineering.lehigh.edu/chbe/graduate/phd-chemical-engineering-phd
What degree do I need to apply to the PhD in Chemical Engineering?
A B.S. or M.S. in chemical engineering or a related engineering discipline is required by matriculation. Related science fields are considered but are less common.
Is the GRE required for the PhD in Chemical Engineering?
No. As of Fall 2020, the Lehigh ChBE program no longer requires submission of GRE scores, and the Rossin College states that the GRE is not required or considered for any of its graduate programs.
What is the application deadline for the PhD in Chemical Engineering?
For fall admission, full applications — including test scores and letters of recommendation — should be submitted no later than Dec. 15. At the college level, PhD applications for fall admission are due December 15 for financial aid consideration, and applications open September 1. Application open dates and deadlines are determined by individual departments. Contact the department concerning relevant deadlines and available start terms.
How much is the application fee?
The application fee is $50 USD. Applications for admission at all levels are completed online through Lehigh’s graduate application portal.
Is the PhD in Chemical Engineering funded?
All PhDs at the Rossin College are 100% fully-funded, however, funding sources may vary by department.
What research areas can I work in as a PhD in Chemical Engineering student?
Research specializations published by the Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering: Energy and the environment; Biomolecular sciences; Functional materials and nanotechnology; Colloidal and interfacial science; Molecular modeling and simulations; Data science, systems, and controls.
What is the qualifying examination for the PhD in Chemical Engineering?
All PhD students must pass a qualification examination given during the second year of residence.
What English proficiency scores are required?
International applicants must meet Lehigh’s minimum scores: TOEFL iBT overall 81 (old scale) or 4 (new scale); IELTS overall 6.5; Duolingo English Test overall 125; Cambridge overall 176; or Pearson (PTE) overall 68. Scores expire two years from the test date. Waivers are available in defined circumstances.
Where is the PhD in Chemical Engineering based?
The Department of Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering is located in HST Building, 124 East Morton Street, Bethlehem, PA 18015, on Lehigh University’s campus in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania.
Who do I contact about the PhD in Chemical Engineering?
The department can be reached at inchegs@lehigh.edu or (610) 758-4261. General Rossin College graduate enquiries go to engineering@lehigh.edu.
